rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_supervised-claude-agentic: proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=3, proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005, img_kernel=7, img_sx=0.5, img_sy=0.5, img_sr=0.02, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.01, optimizer=adam, lambda_neg=1.0, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=800, val_n=200, val_chunk=10, seed=42, rationale=iter-12 dual_domain_bilateral_supervised, re-split Breast-CT val=200. SIX-BOX vs BEST (iter-6 train_n=400/img_n_bf7 hr=0.2555). (1) PRIOR: image BF depth SATURATED (iter-11 img_n_bf=11=0.2555, flat vs 7); proj depth null; kept img_n_bf=7 (same hr, fewer params). ALL architecture axes mapped -> best hr=0.2555. Every iter used only train_n=400 of the 3600-scene pool. (2) Failure mode: a ~24-param BF has almost no capacity to overfit, so more UNIQUE training scenes should mostly help (rarely hurt) generalization on val=200. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 400 -> 800 (best config otherwise: img_n_bf7/img_kernel7/lr1e-2/lneg1.0/ep10). (4) HYPOTHESIS: doubling unique breast scenes gives the trainable sigmas a broader gradient signal and lifts hr above 0.2555 toward ~0.26; if flat, 400 scenes already saturate the tiny BF and iter-13 reverts to 400. (5) BUDGET: 2x train scenes at ep10 -> ~200s, well inside 20 min (train_n=800 <= 2400 cap). (6) Loop continues. Artifacts saved.
